title: Who needs a white card for construction work in Australia, and when does it lapse?
description: Model WHS Regulations r 316 to 318 on general construction induction training: who needs a white card, the 2 year lapse rule, 60 day certification, records.
shortAnswer: Under Part 6.5 of the model Work Health and Safety Regulations, anyone who carries out construction work in Australia must first complete general construction induction training with a Registered Training Organisation and hold a general construction induction training card, known as a white card. A business must not direct or allow construction work by a worker whose training is more than 2 years old if that worker has not done construction work in the preceding 2 years.
keyTakeaways: Regulation 316 requires a person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU) to provide general construction induction training to any worker who has not completed it, or who completed it more than 2 years ago and has not carried out construction work in the preceding 2 years.

Regulation 317 prohibits directing or allowing construction work unless the worker holds a white card, or a training certification issued within the preceding 60 days while the card application is pending.
The card itself has no printed expiry date, but SafeWork NSW states it becomes void after two consecutive years without construction work.
White cards issued under a corresponding WHS law are recognized across jurisdictions (regulation 318) unless cancelled where they were issued.
The white card is a baseline. The model Code of Practice: Construction work expects workplace specific induction and task specific training on top of it.
jurisdiction: Australia (model WHS laws, adopted in all jurisdictions except Victoria)
regulator: Safe Work Australia (model laws) and state and territory WHS regulators, including SafeWork NSW
appliesTo: PCBUs that engage workers to carry out construction work, including builders, principal contractors and subcontractors
Workers carrying out construction work, including managers, engineers, supervisors, surveyors, laborers and tradespeople
People who routinely enter operational construction zones (as described by SafeWork NSW)
Registered Training Organisations delivering the specified construction induction course

sections.heading: What do the model WHS Regulations require for general construction induction?

blocks.text: They require two things: the PCBU must provide general construction induction training to workers who need it, and must not let anyone carry out construction work until that training is complete and current. Both duties sit in Division 1 of Part 6.5 of the [model Work Health and Safety Regulations](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/doc/model-work-health-and-safety-regulations) published by Safe Work Australia, in the version dated December 5, 2025.

Regulation 316 is the duty to provide. It applies where a worker engaged by the PCBU "is to carry out construction work" and either has not successfully completed general construction induction training or completed it more than 2 years previously and has not carried out construction work in the preceding 2 years. Regulation 317(1) is the matching prohibition: the PCBU "must not direct or allow a worker to carry out construction work" unless the training condition is met. Both carry a tier G monetary penalty in the 2025 model text, which replaced the older dollar figures with penalty tiers.

Regulation 317(2) adds an evidence rule. The PCBU must ensure the worker holds a general construction induction training card, or, if the worker has applied for a card but not yet received it, a general construction induction training certification issued within the preceding 60 days. This is the only point at which the regulations accept a paper certificate instead of the card.

blocks.title: Jurisdiction and currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the model WHS Regulations (December 5, 2025 version), the model Code of Practice: Construction work (November 2024) and SafeWork NSW guidance as at November 2026. Model laws only take effect once a jurisdiction adopts them, and Safe Work Australia states that the model laws operate in all jurisdictions except Victoria. Regulation numbers and penalty amounts can differ in each state's own regulation, so check your regulator before relying on a number.

sections.heading: What counts as general construction induction training?

blocks.text: Only training delivered in Australia by a Registered Training Organisation (RTO) for the specified vocational course counts. The model Regulations define general construction induction training as "training delivered in Australia by an RTO for the specified VET course", and define the specified course as Work Safely in the Construction Industry "or a corresponding subsequent VET accredited course". Safe Work Australia's [construction site guidance](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/safety-topic/industry-and-business/construction/working-construction-site) names the current course as 'Prepare to work safely in the construction industry'.

An in-house safety induction, a toolbox talk or an overseas course does not satisfy regulation 317, however thorough it is. The [model Code of Practice: Construction work](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/doc/model-code-practice-construction-work) says the training should cover:

items: the roles, responsibilities and rights of duty holders
health and safety consultation and reporting processes
common construction hazards and control measures
safety information and documentation, for example WHS management plans and safe work method statements (SWMS)

blocks.text: Because the course is a nationally accredited unit, RTOs must assess it under the RTO standards. For how those rules shape assessment, see [Standards for RTOs 2025](/regulations/standards-for-rtos-2025-training-and-assessment).

sections.heading: Does a white card expire, and what is the 2 year rule?

blocks.text: The card carries no expiry date, but the training stops counting once a worker has gone 2 years without construction work. Regulation 320 lists what a card must state: that the holder completed the training, the holder's name, the issue date, a unique identifying number and the issuing state, plus the holder's signature. No expiry date is on that list.

The lapse comes from regulations 316(b) and 317(1)(b). If the training was completed more than 2 years ago, the worker must have carried out construction work in the preceding 2 years. SafeWork NSW puts it more bluntly on its [white cards page](https://www.safework.nsw.gov.au/licences-and-registrations/white-cards): "The white card becomes void if you haven't carried out construction work for two consecutive years or more." A worker in that position must repeat the course before returning to site.

The practical consequence for employers is that holding the card is not enough. To rely on a card older than 2 years, the PCBU needs some evidence that the holder did construction work in the last 2 years, such as previous employment or engagement records.

items: Has the worker completed the specified course with an RTO? If not, provide the training (r 316(a)).
Was it completed within the last 2 years? If yes, the training condition is met.
If older than 2 years, has the worker carried out construction work in the last 2 years? If yes, the condition is met; record the evidence relied on.
If not, the training has lapsed: the worker must not start construction work until retrained (r 316(b), r 317(1)(b)).
Does the worker hold the card, or a certification less than 60 days old with an application pending? If neither, the r 317(2) evidence condition is not met.

sections.heading: How is the white card issued, and what can workers show while they wait?

blocks.text: After the course, the worker or RTO applies to the regulator, and the worker can rely on the training certification for up to 60 days. Under regulation 319, the application must normally be made within 60 days after the certification is issued, and if the regulator has not decided within 60 days the applicant "is taken to hold" a card until a decision is made. Regulation 325 lets a regulator authorize RTOs to issue cards on its behalf.

In New South Wales, SafeWork NSW says applicants must be aged 14 or over and provide the RTO with 100 points of ID. The RTO submits the application and gives the worker a statement of attainment that is valid for 60 days, and SafeWork NSW says most cards are issued within 30 days. NSW also offers an optional digital white card through the Service NSW app, which SafeWork NSW says does not replace the physical card.

sections.heading: Is a white card from another state valid?

blocks.text: Yes, unless the issuing jurisdiction has cancelled it. Regulation 318 says a reference to a general construction induction training card includes "a similar card issued under a corresponding WHS law", and that this does not apply to a card that is cancelled in the corresponding jurisdiction. Safe Work Australia says white cards are recognized Australia-wide, and the Code of Practice adds that an interstate card is valid as long as it is used in accordance with the terms under which it was granted.

sections.heading: What must workers do with their white card?

blocks.text: Workers must keep the card available for inspection, show it to the business engaging them, and must not alter it. Regulation 326 requires a worker carrying out construction work to keep the card, or a pending certification, available for inspection under the Act (tier I penalty), with an exception where the card was lost and a replacement has been applied for. Regulation 327 makes intentionally or recklessly altering a card an offense (tier G). The Code of Practice notes that workers will also need to give the card to the engaging PCBU so the PCBU can be sure the training is complete.

sections.heading: What other induction training does a construction site need?

blocks.text: The Code of Practice expects workplace specific induction and task specific training on top of the white card. Section 6.2 describes workplace specific induction, run by the principal contractor or the PCBU in control of the site, covering items such as site hazards and controls, the location of underground services, the WHS management plan and traffic management plan, site rules, first aid and emergency procedures, and how safety issues are resolved. Section 6.3 adds task specific training, for example on fall arrest equipment, which should be reviewed whenever the task, plant or system of work changes.

Where a site has high risk construction work, workers also need to understand the relevant SWMS. That obligation is covered on the companion page on [SWMS and high risk construction work training](/regulations/construction-swms-and-high-risk-construction-work-training). The general duty to provide information, training and instruction comes from the WHS Act and regulation 39, covered in [what the WHS Act requires](/regulations/whs-act-duty-to-provide-training).

sections.heading: How should a builder evidence white card compliance at audit?

blocks.text: Keep a register that ties each worker to a verified card number, the date checked, and where relevant the evidence of recent construction work. The table below is an original, illustrative mapping of each regulatory duty to the duty holder, the trigger and the evidence an inspector or principal contractor is likely to ask for. sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the construction induction rules as a structured framework: the duties in Part 6.5, the roles they apply to, and the evidence each role must hold. Site induction content and task training are then linked to that framework, so a change to a regulation or a site rule shows which roles and assessments are affected.

faqs.q: Do site visitors need a white card?
faqs.a: The regulations attach the duty to workers who carry out construction work. SafeWork NSW says people who access operational construction zones unaccompanied or not directly supervised by an inducted person may need one, as may workers whose employment causes them to routinely enter those zones. Accompanied visitors usually receive a workplace specific induction instead.

faqs.q: Can a worker start on site with just the statement of attainment?
faqs.a: Yes, for a limited time. Regulation 317(2)(b) accepts a general construction induction training certification issued within the preceding 60 days if the worker has applied for, but not yet been issued, a card. After 60 days the PCBU needs to see the card itself, or rely on the regulator's deemed holding rule if the application is still undecided.

faqs.q: Does online white card training count?
faqs.a: Only if it is delivered by an RTO for the specified VET course and the RTO's delivery and assessment meet the requirements of the course and the regulator. If in doubt, confirm that the provider is an RTO with the course on its scope before signing workers up.

faqs.q: Does the white card apply in Victoria?
faqs.a: Victoria has not adopted the model WHS laws and regulates under its own occupational health and safety legislation, so the regulation numbers on this page do not apply there. The model regulations recognize cards issued under a corresponding WHS law, and Victorian employers should check WorkSafe Victoria's requirements directly.

faqs.q: What should a builder do if a worker's white card is lost?
faqs.a: Regulation 321 lets the holder apply to the regulator for a replacement, and regulation 326(3) relieves the worker of the duty to produce the card while that replacement is pending. The builder should record that the card was previously verified, keep the replacement application reference, and confirm the replacement card once issued.

Regulation 317(2) requires the worker to hold a card or, if applied for but not issued, a certification issued within the preceding 60 days
Regulation 318 recognizes similar cards issued under a corresponding WHS law, except cards cancelled in that jurisdiction
Regulation 319(5) and (8): application within 60 days of certification; applicant taken to hold a card if no decision within 60 days. Regulation 320 lists card content with no expiry date

SafeWork NSW: white card void after two consecutive years without construction work; applicants aged 14 or over; 100 points of ID; statement of attainment valid 60 days; most cards issued within 30 days; digital card optional
Code of Practice s 6.1 lists the training content; s 6.2 lists workplace specific induction topics
